reads.rationale: A domestic share play in Korean skincare is not attractive and the mode call should be read that way. The scorecard scores size 5 (KRW 7.653tn retail, HIGH) but growth 2 — domestic retail is +1.0% YoY (Euromonitor, HIGH) — and porter_skincare rates rivalry HIGH (STRONG) with new-entrant threat HIGH: a near-flat market, a listed duopoly at the top, and near-zero barriers underneath compress economics for anyone buying share. What Korea is genuinely good for is origination, and that is what the mode reflects: partner with the ODM/OEM base (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca — all named, all competing, supplier power LOW) to formulate and fill, and partner into the concentrated shelf (Olive Young holds >85% of the H&B store market at 1,380+ stores, and rtm_KR reads it as a near-gatekeeper). That is an asset-light presence that produces corridor-ready product, not a domestic share contest.
reads.alternatives_considered: build was rejected: owning production in the world's densest contract-manufacturing market duplicates capacity that is already commoditised, into +1% domestic demand. acquire has no grounding — the repo records no KR skincare M&A transaction to benchmark a multiple against (the only exit multiple on file, HUL/Minimalist at 8.5x, is Indian). import_corridor is directionally wrong: the corridor in this dataset runs KR->IN, and Korea is its source, so corridor_tailwind is literally null on every KR row.

reads.rationale: India skincare is the largest documented prize in the dataset (US$9.06bn RETAIL, LOW) with the richest channel access (score 4, STRONG) and a strong corridor pull (score 4, STRONG: HS 3304 imports from Korea US$0.14bn in 2024, K-brands across Nykaa and Blinkit). But an unaided import play buys the most contested shelf at the highest take. porter_skincare rates IN rivalry HIGH (STRONG) and buyer power HIGH: Nykaa charges 22-26% on skincare plus GST, q-commerce runs ~38% all-in on MRP, and the Blinkit snapshot shows the conglomerate K-brands already deeply stocked (The Face Shop 21 SKUs, Laneige 16, Innisfree 9) — the general K-skincare slot is taken. The defensible mode is therefore partnering into a conduit rather than arriving alone: the evidenced entry pattern is the platform relationship itself (Nykaa's 10-year AmorePacific tie-up; Tira's 2026 exclusive-launch sprint), which buys placement and marketing weight the entrant cannot self-fund against a 22-28% take.
reads.alternatives_considered: import_corridor unaided is the obvious alternative and remains viable on the demand evidence, but it lands into HIGH rivalry and HIGH buyer power with no shelf guarantee and a 3-9 month CDSCO wait ahead of first revenue (regulatory.json) — the reason it is second, not first. build via India contract manufacturing (the Limese/Pilgrim Korean-ingredient template, MOQs ~500 units) escapes CDSCO entirely and is credible at mass Rs500-700 price points, but forfeits Korean-origin authenticity, which is the entrant's only differentiator here. acquire is unsupported: the sole India beauty exit benchmark on file is HUL/Minimalist at ~8.5x revenue, which prices consolidation richly and is a dermocosmetics, not general-skincare, datapoint.

reads.rationale: The cleanest corridor import case after dermocosmetics, and it scores 3.5 on all 6 criteria. Demand pull is specific and evidenced rather than inferred: 'Korean sunscreen' searches +148% and 'glass skin' +61% in a quarter, top Korean brands +50% on Nykaa, Nykaa platform sunscreen sales +85% YoY, and Beauty of Joseon's Relief Sunscreen (Rs1,570 MRP) a category bestseller — consumers are already asking for Korean-origin SPF by name, which is exactly the demand an import play monetises and a domestic build cannot claim. The category is underpenetrated (baseline whitespace #2) and rising fastest on the access rail (q-commerce sunscreen projected +170% in 2026), so the shelf is expanding rather than defended. Regulatory friction is now quantified and manageable: a narrow SPF hero range from a single Korean ODM plant registers for roughly USD 1,000-2,000 per category plus USD 50/variant and USD 500/site, on a 3-9 month clock, against a COS-2 valid 5 years.
reads.alternatives_considered: build (domestic sunscreen manufacture) is genuinely feasible — India has a large sunscreen base and supplier power is LOW — and it sidesteps CDSCO, but it discards the Korean-origin signal the search and Nykaa data show is doing the selling. partner with a conduit is the closest second and can be layered on top: the q-commerce whitespace is a distribution problem, not a registration problem. acquire is unsupported — no India sun-care acquisition is recorded in the repo.

reads.rationale: Scored on all 6 criteria but the lowest composite in the dataset (2.5), and the mode has to be read alongside a blunt finding: there is effectively no KR->IN fragrance corridor. HS 3303 imports from Korea were US$0.000135bn in 2024 and no Korean fragrance brand entry is recorded — corridor_tailwind scores 1 on evidenced near-absence, so a Korean-origin entrant has no advantage in this segment at all. What the evidence does support, for an entrant generally, is a domestic build: mass perfume and deodorant are filled domestically through contract manufacturing (supplier power LOW at mass, new-entrant threat HIGH), D2C fragrance is actively funded, and the incumbent concentration is a single KKR-controlled leader (Vini/Fogg, INR 1,200cr FY25) rather than a wall of MNCs. The premium tier is the part to avoid on an import basis: porter records it as import-reliant on UAE, France and Germany for oils and finished goods — supply routes that run through the Gulf, not Korea.
reads.alternatives_considered: import_corridor is rejected on direct evidence, not judgement — the KR->IN fragrance trade flow is effectively zero. partner with a conduit is weak because fragrance-specific channel depth is missing (only a Nykaa 22-25% commission datapoint exists; GT/MT and gifting weight are unrecorded), so there is no conduit case to partner into. acquire is unsupported — the only ownership datapoint is KKR's 54% of Vini, a control position at a scale that is not an entry vehicle.

reads.rationale: Scored on 3 of 6 criteria (composite 3.3) and carrying the firmest growth signal in the Korean dataset: +13% YoY 2024 at HIGH confidence (Euromonitor), driven by an actives race (PDRN, exosomes, peptides). Unlike KR skincare, this is not a flat market — but it is still not a domestic share play an outsider wins by building, because porter_dermocosmetics rates rivalry HIGH with the majors holding derma brands (AmorePacific's Aestura and Illiyoon) atop a broad indie and ODM base. The route the evidence supports is partner: the ODM base extends into actives-heavy derma formulation (supplier power LOW), and MFDS approval is cheap and fast where a formulation reuses pre-approved functional actives (~7 days, ~KRW 189,000) — so partnering for formulation and shelf gives access to the actives frontier without owning either. The strategic case is compounded by the corridor: a KR derma position is the supply side of India's highest-conviction whitespace.
reads.alternatives_considered: build is weakened by the same ODM depth that makes partnering cheap, and by the one real supplier caveat porter flags — frontier actives are the exception to LOW supplier power. acquire is unsupported: no KR derma transaction or multiple is recorded (APR/Medicube appears in the data as an India entrant, not as an acquisition target with a price). A domestic share contest is rejected on rivalry HIGH plus a definitionally unresolved market size (Korean sources ~4x apart, KRW 1.2tn to KRW 4.5tn).

reads.rationale: The layer's headline entry case and the highest-conviction import call in the dataset. It scores 3.5 on all 6 criteria with the strongest corridor tailwind in the taxonomy (5, STRONG): baseline whitespace #1 is mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3, Nykaa K-beauty GMV is +60% YoY (Q3 2025, MEDIUM), and a 2026 launch wave is already landing (Medicube on Nykaa and Tira, Illiyoon Nykaa-exclusive, Aestura, Dr. Melaxin exclusive to Tira). Competitive openness is 4 (STRONG) with a proven exit benchmark — Minimalist at INR 347cr FY24 revenue acquired by HUL at INR 2,955cr, ~8.5x — showing the category creates real value. The import route is the right one specifically because the whitespace is Korean-origin derma: corridor_vector reads the corridor as an import-and-curate route, noting even AmorePacific is scaling India through platforms and imports with no India plant announced. The single real cost is CDSCO, and regulatory.json now sizes it: roughly USD 1,000-2,000 per category plus USD 50/variant and USD 500/site, 3-9 months to COS-2, valid 5 years — a lead-time and working-capital cost, not a barrier, and one that argues for a tight hero-SKU range from a single ODM plant. The gap to attack is dark-store distribution, where the Blinkit snapshot shows conglomerate brands deep-stocked while indie derma (COSRX out-of-stock, Anua 'coming soon', Some By Mi absent) is missing.
reads.alternatives_considered: partner with a conduit is the necessary complement rather than a rival — the import decision reduces to conduit choice, with Nykaa ranked first (deepest Korean assortment, the only conduit with a published corridor demand signal) and Tira second on its exclusive-launch model. build via India contract manufacturing avoids CDSCO entirely and is the Limese/Pilgrim template, but a made-in-India derma line surrenders the Korean-origin claim that is the whole basis of the +60% GMV pull, and drops into the most contested lane in Indian beauty (rivalry HIGH, STRONG). acquire is priced against a single benchmark (8.5x revenue) that reflects a strategic FMCG buyer, and there is no evidence of available India derma assets at entry scale.
